model: DeepSeek V4 Flash REAP 150B (puwaer/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-reap-150b, 132 routed experts, fp4 experts / fp8 dense), colibri safetensors layout, 78.9 GiB on disk
command: build: cd c && make -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr NVCC=/usr/bin/nvcc CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1 -j8; run: python3 c/coli serve --model <REAP dir> --ram 40 --ctx 8192 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090, server environment exactly PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/LANG + the config's env keys (env -i); one freshly started server process per sample; 3 samples per arm D0/G1/R1/X3 interleaved with the order rotated per round (D0 s1 G1 s1 R1 s1 X3 s1 G1 s2 R1 s2 X3 s2 D0 s2 R1 s3 X3 s3 D0 s3 G1 s3); client bench_decode.py sends 6 prompts one after another, max_tokens 300 each, streamed (the engine is greedy: temperature is ignored); per-sample tok_s = mean over the 6 prompts of (chunks - 1) / (last chunk - first chunk); baseline arm R1, trial arm X3

notes.dev_vs_pr2_off: D0 (upstream dev) vs G1 (pr2 tip, every PR2 switch off, V4_SERVE_STATS_LOG=1): median 3.0113 vs 2.9830 tok/s (-0.94%), texts identical. Not a manifest: more than one variable differs (the whole PR1+PR2 code, and the stats log). The likely cause is PR1's batched-prefill bank: with COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1 (set for every arm) the pr2 tip reserves VRAM for the 132-slot bank (serve.log mirror-reserve=3100MiB), while dev refuses the batch path for 132 experts and reserves none (no mirror-reserve line); GPU0 peak memory.used D0 22008 MiB vs G1 21192 MiB, i.e. ~816 MiB fewer decode mirrors. The reserve can be lowered with DSV4_CUDA_VRAM_RESERVE_MB; a decode-only server can leave COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH unset.
